groups.defect: In the uniqueGuests filter of addGuests.handler.ts, guest emails are compared case-sensitively against the lowercased blacklist and against existing attendee emails. Changing the case of an address lets it bypass the blacklist or be added again as a duplicate attendee. Normalizing emails in that filter fixes both.

answer.reasoning: All three suggestions point at the same few lines (70-78) and the same cause: the submitted guest email is never normalized before it is compared. s_0f78e9fc and s_969329e8 name two effects, the blacklist bypass and duplicate attendees. s_2eda8d39 leads with the blacklist bypass, but its fix says to apply the normalized value to the duplicate checks too. So it covers the attendee comparison, and posting it next to the others would be redundant. One normalization change in that one filter resolves all three. A stricter reading could treat the duplicate-attendee issue as a second defect that s_2eda8d39 only mentions in its fix, which would make it a partial overlap. That makes this a judgment call.
